title: Battle of Plataea
description: Added from the Generations curriculum import (Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020)). Dated only by the Generations books cited below; no tier 1–4 chronology covers this event.

sorting_basis.note: PROVISIONAL: no CFAH, Ussher–Jones or Ussher date exists, so the sort uses Generations (Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), PDF p. 547): 479 BC. Pending owner decision (open question A8).

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (1st ed., 2020), ch. 12 "The Kingdom of the Medes and Persians (725–330 BC)", PDF p. 380 (printed p. 379)
chronologies.edition_note: 1st ed. (2020); superseded by the 2nd ed. (2024), which prints "479 BC" (PDF p. 547): the same date.

chronologies.citation: Preparing the World for Jesus (2nd ed., 2024), ch. 20 "The Kingdoms of the Elamites, the Medes, and the Persians", PDF p. 547 (printed p. 533)

chronologies.date: “he thought it best to winter in Thessaly, and wait for the spring before he attempted the Peloponnese”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 8.113 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 561 (PDF p. 563)
chronologies.note: Mardonius winters in Thessaly after Salamis; the land war resumes the next year. DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): The next spring is 479 BC (CFAH AP-13 480 BC + 1).

chronologies.date: “It was ten months after the taking of the city by the king that Mardonius came against it for the second time”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 9.3 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 576 (PDF p. 578)
chronologies.note: DERIVED (not Herodotus's figure): About ten months after Xerxes took Athens in 480 BC (8.51, AP-13): mid 479 BC. Agrees with CFAH-3 (AP-13): "The Second Persian Invasion of Greece ended in June 479 B.C., about 15 months after it began." Generations: 479 BC (provisional).

chronologies.date: “That the two battles were really fought on the same day of the same month”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 9.101 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 620 (PDF p. 622)
chronologies.note: Plataea and Mycale on the same day (Mycale has no record; NEW candidate).

chronologies.date: “And this was all that took place that year.”
chronologies.citation: Herodotus, Histories 9.121 (tr. George Rawlinson; Roman Roads Media etext, 2013), p. 628 (PDF p. 630)
chronologies.note: The last sentence of the narrative: the year of Plataea, Mycale and the siege of Sestos.
